{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -l select=1:ncpus=64:mpiprocs=4:mem=1GB
#   -l walltime=00:05:00
#   -q short_cpuQ
#   -N md_64_4
#   -o md_64_4_out
#   -e md_64_4_err

# Map: 1 node, 4 MPI ranks, 64 CPUs total => 16 cores per rank.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 16
#flux: --time-limit=5m
#flux: --job-name=md_64_4
#flux: --output=md_64_4_out
#flux: --error=md_64_4_err

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=1GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -q short_cpuQ (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# PBS variable $PBS_O_WORKDIR is not set under Flux.
# Use the directory where `flux batch` was invoked.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

module load gcc91
module load openmpi-3.0.0
module load BLAS
module load gsl-2.5
module load lapack-3.7.0
module load cuda-11.3

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/home/giuseppe.gambini/usr/installations/plumed/lib
source /home/giuseppe.gambini/usr/src/gmx_plumed.sh

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16

# PBS used mpirun; under Flux, use flux-run to launch MPI ranks.
flux run -n 4 -c 16 /home/giuseppe.gambini/usr/installations/gromacs/bin/gmx_mpi mdrun -s ../../md.tpr
"
}
